title: Getting Your Property Cited in AI Answers and Voice Search
excerpt: How hotels and homestays can appear in Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini and voice search with answer-first FAQs, structured data, consistent facts and detailed reviews.
description: Get your hotel cited in AI answers and voice search: answer-first FAQs, LodgingBusiness and FAQ schema, consistent listing facts and review content.
html:
To get your property cited in AI answers and voice search, publish clear, factual answers to the questions guests ask, keep your details identical across your website, Google Business Profile and OTA listings, add structured data such as LodgingBusiness and FAQ markup, and earn detailed reviews. These tools generally draw on sources that are clear, consistent and trusted.

How AI answers and voice assistants find information

Guests increasingly ask questions rather than type keywords: "quiet homestay near Chikmagalur with a coffee estate walk", "pet-friendly resort within three hours of Bengaluru", "Hey Google, call the nearest hotel with parking". The answer may come from Google's AI Overviews, a chat assistant such as ChatGPT or Gemini, or a voice assistant on a phone or smart speaker.

The exact methods these systems use are not public, and they change. What can be said in general terms:

  • Google's AI Overviews draw on pages from Google's search index, so the usual basics of being indexed and useful still apply.
  • Chat assistants that browse the web retrieve pages and summarise them, and some show links to the sources they used.
  • Voice assistants often answer local questions from business listings such as Google Business Profile, and read out short answers.
  • All of them are more likely to use information that is stated clearly, matches across sources and comes from sites that appear reliable.

There is no special switch for "AI SEO". The practical work is making your facts easy to find, easy to quote and consistent everywhere.

Write answer-first content

An AI system or voice assistant usually needs a short, direct answer it can lift from your page. Most hotel websites bury facts in descriptive paragraphs. Rewrite key pages so the answer comes first and the detail follows.

Guest questionWeak answerAnswer-first version
Is the property pet-friendly?"We love animals and welcome all our guests' companions""Yes, dogs are allowed in our garden cottages for a cleaning fee of ₹500 per stay. Please tell us when booking."
How far is it from the airport?"Conveniently located near major transport links""We are 42 km from Mangaluru airport, about 75 minutes by car. We can arrange a pickup."
What time is check-in?"Flexible arrangements available""Check-in is from 1 pm and checkout by 11 am. Early check-in depends on availability."

The figures in the right-hand column are placeholders; use your own. Apply this style to your homepage introduction, room pages, location page and policies.

Build a proper FAQ section

Most guest questions arrive on WhatsApp and the phone. Those are your FAQ. Collect the last few months of enquiries and pick the questions that come up most often. Typical ones:

  • Check-in and checkout times; early check-in and late checkout.
  • Cancellation and refund policy.
  • Whether meals are included, and food options (veg, Jain, non-veg, children's meals).
  • Pets, children, extra beds, accessibility.
  • Parking, EV charging, how to reach from the airport, station and main city.
  • Wi-Fi, power backup, mobile network coverage.
  • Payment methods, including UPI, and whether an advance is needed.
  • Nearby attractions and distances.

Write each answer in two to four sentences, starting with the direct answer. Keep the FAQ on your website, visible on the page (not only in a downloadable PDF), and update it when policies change.

Structured data, explained simply

Structured data is a small block of code on your web pages that labels facts in a format search engines understand: this is the property name, this is the address, this is the phone number, these are the check-in times. Guests do not see it, but it removes guesswork for machines.

Two types worth knowing

  • LodgingBusiness (or a more specific type such as Hotel or BedAndBreakfast) from Schema.org describes your property: name, address, phone, geographic coordinates, check-in and checkout times, amenities, price range and links to your official profiles.
  • FAQPage marks up questions and answers that appear on the page. Google has limited where FAQ rich results are shown in search, so do not expect a visual change in results; the markup still labels your answers clearly.

Your developer can add these. The rules are simple: mark up only what is visible on the page, keep it accurate and update it when details change. Google's Rich Results Test lets you check the code is valid. Our SEO and organic growth page explains how this sits alongside other technical work.

Make your facts consistent everywhere

If your website says check-in is at 12 pm, Google Business Profile says 2 pm and your Booking.com listing says 1 pm, any system summarising your property has to guess, and a guest who trusts the wrong one will be unhappy. Audit your facts across every place they appear:

  • Your website (every page, including old blog posts and PDFs).
  • Google Business Profile, including hours, attributes, description and Q&A.
  • OTA listings: MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Booking.com, Agoda, Airbnb.
  • Social profiles: Instagram bio, Facebook page.
  • Directories and tourism listings that mention you.

Check, at minimum: property name spelling, address, phone and WhatsApp number, check-in and checkout times, pet and child policies, meal plans, distances, and amenities. Our post on OTA listing optimisation covers the listing side in more depth.

Reviews are content too

Reviews on Google, OTAs and travel sites are among the most detailed information that exists about your property, written by people who stayed. They often mention exactly the things guests ask about: the view, the food, the road, the noise, the Wi-Fi. Assistants that summarise properties can draw on that kind of material.

  • Ask every satisfied guest for a review, and suggest they mention what they enjoyed most.
  • Reply to every review, adding factual detail where helpful ("yes, the last 2 km is a mud road; we now send a map before arrival").
  • Fix recurring complaints; repeated mentions shape how your property is described.
  • Never write fake reviews or offer incentives for positive ones.

For a fuller approach, see our guide to reputation management for resorts.

Optimising for voice specifically

Voice questions are usually local and immediate: "near me", "open now", "call". Voice assistants commonly rely on business listings for these, so a complete, accurate Google Business Profile matters most. Make sure your hours (including 24-hour reception if you have it), phone number and category are right. Spoken answers are short, which is another reason to keep your answer-first sentences brief and plain.

Frequently asked questions

Can I pay to appear in AI answers or Google AI Overviews?

You cannot pay to be included as a cited source in AI Overviews or in organic answers from chat assistants. Some platforms show ads near or within AI features, but that is separate advertising. Being cited depends on having clear, accurate, useful information that the system can find and trust.

Does structured data guarantee my property will be cited?

No. Structured data helps search engines understand your facts, but it does not guarantee any particular display or citation. It works best alongside clear on-page content, consistent details across listings and good reviews. Mark up only what is visible on the page and keep it accurate.

How do I check what AI tools say about my property?

Ask them the questions a guest would ask, such as "is [property name] pet-friendly?" or "best homestays near [place]", in ChatGPT, Gemini and Google search. Note any wrong facts, then find where that information appears online and correct it at the source, starting with your website and Google Business Profile.

Is voice search worth worrying about for a small homestay?

The work is the same work that helps every other channel: an accurate Google Business Profile, clear answers on your website and consistent facts everywhere. You do not need a separate voice strategy. If those basics are right, you are as prepared for voice queries as you reasonably can be.

Where to start

Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google five questions a guest might ask about your property and note anything wrong or missing. Compare your check-in times, policies and contact details across your website, Google Business Profile and OTA listings, and correct any mismatch. Then rewrite your ten most common WhatsApp questions as an answer-first FAQ on your site.
